BEFORE  HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE B. P. SHARMA  ON THE 6 th OF MARCH, 2026  MISC. CRIMINAL CASE No. 55392 of 2023  UMESH KUMAR NEMA  Versus  THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH AND OTHERS

Appearance:
 Shri Prakash Upadhyay, Sr. Adv. along with Shri Jalaj   Advocate for petitioner.
Shri Mohan Lal Sharma - Advocate for the respondent/In  Ms. Nitu Pasine - Panel Lawyer for respondent/State.

ORDER By way of the present petition filed under Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita,
2023 (corresponding to Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure), the petitioner seeks quashment of the entire criminal proceedings in Sessions Trial No. 1/2023, as well as the order dated 20.11.2023 passed in the said sessions trial, whereby charges have been framed against the petitioner/accused for the offences punishable under Section 419, 420, 467, 468 and 120B of the Indian Penal Code.
2.

As per the FIR (Annexure A/1), the complainant Surjanbai lodged a written report alleging that accused Rahul, in connivance with the then Patwari Gangaram, falsely represented that the land bearing Survey No. 133, admeasuring 5.492 hectares, situated at village Narwara, belonged to him.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:21969 2 MCRC-55392-2023

On the basis of such misrepresentation, accused Rahul obtained a loan of Rs. 2,33,000/- from Union Bank of India,
Branch Gotegaon.

During the course of investigation, it was revealed that accused Rahul, in collusion with the then Patwari Gangaram, prepared forged revenue documents (khasra entries)
relating to the said land and, on the strength of such fabricated documents, secured the aforesaid loan from the bank.

It has further been revealed that the present petitioner/co-accused prepared the search report and the spot verification report in connection with the loan transaction, whereas in reality the said land was recorded in the names of complainant Surjanbai, Premabai and other persons, and did not belong to accused Rahul.
On the basis of these allegations, the present criminal proceedings came to be initiated.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the petitioner has been falsely implicated in the present case.
It is contended that there is no direct or indirect evidence on record to show any involvement of the petitioner with the beneficiary in obtaining approval of the loan from the bank.

It is further submitted that the petitioner, being an Advocate engaged by the bank, was responsible only for rendering legal services and performing legal work in connection with loan transactions,
and therefore he cannot be held responsible for the sanction of the loan granted by the bank.
It is also submitted that no specific allegations have been made against the petitioner in the FIR, nor was the petitioner ever called during the course of investigation.

According to the petitioner, he has neither prepared any forged document nor had any intention to deceive any person for the purpose of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:21969 3 MCRC-55392-2023 extending undue benefit to anyone.

Learned counsel further submits that the petitioner has been implicated solely on the basis that he prepared the search report and issued the non-encumbrance certificate, which were appended with the loan sanction documents.

It is contended that the khasra documents relating to the land were duly verified by the Tehsildar, Gotegaon, and the concerned Patwari, and stamp tickets affixed thereon were in the name of Sovaran Singh Lodhi.
It is thus argued that the petitioner had relied upon the official revenue records and documents produced before him while rendering his legal opinion.
It is further submitted that no material has been placed on record by the complainant to substantiate the allegation of criminal conspiracy punishable under Section 120B of the Indian Penal Code.

Learned counsel has also contended that the legal opinion or professional services rendered by an Advocate, given in the course of his professional duties in good faith and without any mens rea, cannot be treated as an act constituting a criminal offence.
Therefore, it is prayed that the entire criminal proceedings against the petitioner be quashed.

4. The learned Government Advocate appearing for the State opposed the petition and submitted that the present petitioner had a significant role in facilitating the loan transaction by preparing the search report and spot verification report, which constituted the basis for processing and sanctioning the loan.

It is contended that the petitioner, being a legal professional engaged by the bank, was under a duty to exercise proper due diligence and verify the title of the property before issuing such reports.

However, despite the fact that the land in question was not recorded in the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:21969 4 MCRC-55392-2023 name of accused Rahul,
the petitioner submitted reports which ultimately enabled the accused to obtain the loan from the bank.

It is further submitted on behalf of the State that the question as to whether the petitioner acted negligently or in deliberate collusion with the co-accused can only be determined after proper appreciation of evidence during the course of trial.

At the stage of exercising inherent jurisdiction under Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (corresponding to Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure), the Court is not required to undertake a detailed evaluation of the evidence or consider the defence put forth by the accused.

It is also contended that the allegations contained in the charge- sheet disclose the commission of offences punishable under Section 419 of the Indian Penal Code, Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code, Section 467 of the Indian Penal Code, Section 468 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 120B of the Indian Penal Code.
The Trial Court has already found prima facie material on record while framing charges against the petitioner.
Therefore, interference by this Court at this stage would not be justified.

sentences.text: This Court has bestowed its anxious consideration to the rival submissions advanced by learned counsel for the parties and the law governing the exercise of inherent jurisdiction under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

6. The inherent jurisdiction of this Court under Section 482 Cr.P.C. is required to be exercised sparingly and with great circumspection, only in cases where the allegations, even if taken at their face value, do not disclose the commission of any offence, or where continuation of the proceedings NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:21969 5 MCRC-55392-2023 would amount to abuse of the process of law.

This principle has been consistently reiterated by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal, 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335.
7.

entities.text: State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal, 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This Court has carefully perused the record of the case and the material collected during the course of investigation.

From the case diary it appears that the then Branch Manager, Rajeev Tiwari,
had carried out the spot verification in connection with the loan transaction, whereas the present petitioner, who is an Advocate, had prepared the search report relating to the title of the property.
It is also apparent from the record that the petitioner has been specifically named in the FIR.

Further,
Thakurdas Parihar, Branch Manager of Union Bank of India, Branch Gotegaon, in his statement recorded under Section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, has stated that the search report in respect of the property was prepared by the present petitioner.

Apart from this, the report of Patwari, Halka No.57, which forms part of the case record, indicates that the land bearing Survey No.133 is recorded in the names of Surjanbai and others, and not in the name of accused Rahul Lodhi, who had obtained the loan from the bank by representing himself to be the owner of the said land.

Further, in the statement of the complainant Surjanbai recorded during investigation on 25.11.2015, she has specifically alleged that accused Rahul Lodhi, in connivance with Patwari Gangaram Patel, Advocate Umesh Nema (the present petitioner) and Branch Manager Rajeev Tiwari, prepared false and fabricated documents in respect of the said land.

It has further been alleged that on the basis of such forged documents, accused Rahul Lodhi obtained a NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:21969 6 MCRC-55392-2023 loan of Rs.2,33,000/- from the aforesaid bank by showing his mother Urmila Singh as the guarantor.
Similar statement has been given by prosecution witnesses Ramkrishna Mehra, Prembai and Thakurdas.
In view of the aforesaid material collected during investigation, it cannot be conclusively held at this stage that the petitioner had no role in the alleged transaction.

8. It is also pertinent to note that the then Branch Manager, Rajeev Tiwari, who is also an accused in the present case, had earlier approached this Court by filing a petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure registered as M.Cr.C. No. 47855 of 2022, seeking quashment of the same criminal proceedings.
The said petition was dismissed by this Court vide order dated 10.07.2023.
Thus, the proceedings in the Sessions Trial have already been permitted to continue against the said co-accused.

9. Learned counsel for the petitioner has relied upon the decision of the Supreme Court in CBI,
Hyderabad v. K. Narayana Rao (2012) 9 SCC 512 to submit that an advocate who renders professional services by giving a legal opinion or report cannot be fastened with criminal liability in the absence of any material showing his involvement in a criminal conspiracy.

However, this Court Umesh Kumar Nema vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7987062/
3 finds that the aforesaid judgment is not applicable to the facts of the present case.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said decision, the Supreme Court observed that a panel advocate of a bank cannot be prosecuted merely on the ground that the legal opinion furnished by him later turned out to be incorrect, unless there exists material to indicate that the advocate had knowledge of the fraudulent transaction or had consciously participated in the conspiracy.

In NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:21969 7 MCRC-55392-2023 the case at hand, the material collected during investigation prima facie reveals that the search report concerning the property was prepared by the present petitioner, which constituted one of the bases for the processing of the loan.

The record further indicates, as reflected in the report of the Patwari, Halka No.57, that the land bearing Survey No.133 was recorded in the names of Surjanbai and others, and not in the name of accused Rahul.
Notwithstanding this, the loan transaction was processed on the basis of the reports and documents submitted in relation to the said property.

In the statement of the complainant Surjanbai recorded during investigation on 25.11.2015, she has specifically alleged that accused Rahul Lodhi, in connivance with Patwari Gangaram Patel, Advocate Umesh Nema (the present petitioner) and Branch Manager Rajeev Tiwari, prepared false and fabricated documents in respect of the said land.

Prosecution witnesses Ramkrishna Mehra, Prembai and Thakurdas have also given similar statement, which indicates about conspiracy to fabricate forged agricultural document for the purpose of obtaining bank loan.
10. Thus at this stage, it cannot be conclusively determined that the petitioner had no role in the alleged transaction.

Whether the petitioner had merely discharged his professional duties in good faith or whether he acted negligently or in connivance with the other accused persons done intentionally are questions which require appreciation of evidence and can only be adjudicated during the course of trial.

In these circumstances, the principle laid down in CBI, Hyderabad v. K.
Narayana Rao (supra) does not advance the case of the petitioner at this stage, and the present matter does NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:21969 8 MCRC-55392-2023 not fall within the parameters warranting quashment of criminal proceedings.

CBI, Hyderabad v. K.
Narayana Rao
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
11. In view of the foregoing discussion and upon consideration of the material available on record,
this Court is of the opinion that the allegations made in the FIR and the material collected during the course of investigation disclose prima facie involvement of the petitioner in the alleged transaction.

The questions raised by the petitioner pertain to disputed facts and appreciation of evidence, which cannot be adjudicated in exercise of inherent jurisdiction under Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (corresponding to Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure).
At this stage, it cannot be said that continuation of the criminal proceedings would amount to an abuse of the process of the Court.
12. Accordingly, no case is made out for quashment of the impugned proceedings.
The present petition being devoid of merits is hereby dismissed.
However, it is clarified that any observation made herein is only for the purpose of deciding the present petition and shall not prejudice the trial Court while deciding the case on its own merits.

13. Pending application(s), if any stands closed.
